description.narrative: Denna isats rör projektstöd till Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Centre (KAIPTC), specifikt avdelningen med namnet Women and Youth Peace and Security Institute, WYPSI. Det övergripande syftet är att stärka kvinnor och ungas bidrag till arbetet för hållbar fred och säkerhet i Afrika. Insatsen följer tidigare projektstöd under perioden 2019-2023. Programmet sköts ifrån KAIPTCs kontor i Accra, Ghana.

This contribution concerns support to the Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Centre (KAIPTC), more specifically support to the Women and Youth Peace and Security Institute (WYPSI). The overall goal of the project is "To enhance the role of women and youth to contribute to achieving sustainable peace and security in Africa". The planned contribution follows previous support to the programme "Enhancing the Operationalization of the Women, Peace and Security Agenda in Africa", with a budget of 15 MSEK over three years (2019­2023). As for the previous support, KAIPTC will be the direct and only recipient of the funding for this planned contribution and the programme will be managed from its office based in Accra, Ghana.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative: Narrate Key Achievements thematically, as documented in the 2024 narrative report: a.The theoretical knowledge of grassroots women in Ghana was significantly enhanced to expedite the implementation of the Women, Peace, and Security (WPS) agenda at the community level. Targeted trainees empowered women to actively participate in peacebuilding and advocacy efforts. This initiative bolstered the capacity of grassroots women to become key drivers of the WPS agenda within their communities. b.Stakeholder consultative meetings in Kenya, Uganda, Nigeria, Senegal, and Ghana effectively identified challenges, opportunities, and actionable recommendations to progress Africas Youth, Peace, and Security (YPS) agenda. These engagements brought together a diverse range of stakeholders, fostering dialogue to tackle gaps such as limited youth inclusion, gender disparities, and insufficient institutional coordination. Key outcomes, including a validated roadmap and actionable recommendations, established a solid foundation for integrating YPS into education, utilising technology for peacebuilding, and enhancing interregional collaboration. Following up on this, the Symposium served as a platform for sharing best practices across the continent even beyond the physical engagement. c.The capacity of a cross section of local actors engaged in GBV issues in Benin was enhanced to address Gender-Based Violence (GBV) more effectively. Traditional and religious leaders were sensitised and educated to refer GBV cases to appropriate authorities rather than resolving them within communities. This approach would contribute to promoting accountability, strengthening institutional responses, and reducing the prevalence of GBV in Benin. d.Through comprehensive election observation training, 144 election observers were equipped to monitor 1,066 polling stations in six regions of Ghana, focusing on gender and age-disaggregated situations related to election management, security, and results collation. Real-time information from observers on the ground supported effective decision-making at the Womens Situation Room, enabling timely responses to incidents during the elections. This initiative strengthened gender-sensitive election monitoring and advocacy, with mediators and observers playing pivotal roles in ensuring a peaceful electoral process. The Election Observation Training by KAIPTC received overwhelmingly positive feedback, with 76.74% of participants rating it as "Excellent," 20.93% as "Very Good," and only 2.33% as "Good," with no "Fair" or "Poor" ratings. This indicates that approximately 100% of the participants expressed satisfaction about the content of the training. Participants suggested extending training sessions, collaborating with youth organizations, enhancing communication strategies, leveraging social media, and providing more training materials. The program effectively enhanced participants' understanding of election observation principles, boosted their confidence in monitoring elections, and strengthened their skills in conflict prevention and reporting. The positive feedback underscores the programs success in preparing observers for Ghanas 2024 general elections. e.The analysis indicates that the majority of respondents felt highly confident in applying the knowledge and skills gained from the course, with 52.9% reporting being "Extremely Confident" and 47.1% being "Confident," while none expressed uncertainty or lack of confidence. The post-training evaluation showed that all participants demonstrated above-average performance in knowledge levels, with 64.8% achieving "High" performance levels and 35.2% reaching "Extremely High" levels, with no scores in the "Average", "Low" or "Extremely Low" categoriesdemonstrating a 100% improvement in knowledge levels. Overall, targeted exposure to election-related topics significantly enhanced participants' understanding of electoral violence, conflict analysis, election dispute management, and mediation, with notable gains in election security, communication, and conflict resolution techniques. The results underscore the effectiveness of the training in deepening participants' grasp of election complexities while highlighting areas for further development and recommending the integration of instant impact assessments in future programs.
